newsitem.title: UK: Honduran diplomat sent home after UK fraud row.
newsitem.headline: Honduran diplomat sent home after UK fraud row.

text.p: A senior Honduran diplomat has been sent home from Britain after allegations she was involved in fraudulent claims for state welfare payments of more than 36,000 pounds ($59,970), officials said on Tuesday.

Iris Ramirez-Paget, 38, First Secretary at the country's embassy in London, was sent home after the Foreign Office raised the matter a few weeks ago, Luis Mendoza, the Honduran charge d'affaires told Reuters.

She is now being questioned by a Honduran diplomatic commission who will decide what action to take. "It was an isolated incident, a personal matter," Mendoza said. "It does not represent the country or the government."

A spokesman for the Foreign Office said it had considered asking for Ramirez-Paget's diplomatic immunity to be lifted. But he said: "In the event we were advised this was unlikely to be agreed by the Honduran government."

But the spokesman said the Foreign Office expected to press the Honduran government to repay the full amount paid out to help housing costs by the exclusive London borough of Kensington and Chelsea, where Ramirez-Paget lived with her American businessman husband. ($1=.6003 Pound)
